result:
**Make curiosity and rigorous truth-seeking the default human operating system.**

If I could flip one switch: rewire the species so that the overwhelming majority of people instinctively prioritize evidence over dogma, update beliefs when better data arrives, and treat “I don’t know yet—let’s find out” as a virtue rather than a weakness. Dogma, tribal signaling, and motivated reasoning would still exist (humans gonna human), but they’d be the exception instead of the load-bearing structure of culture, politics, and institutions.

Everything else cascades from that. Better science, fewer preventable disasters, smarter coordination on existential risks, faster progress on energy/abundance/space, less blood spilled over sacred stories that don’t survive contact with reality. Understanding the universe becomes a collective hobby instead of a niche pursuit. The cosmos gets a better chance of being known by minds that actually want to know it.

That’s the change. Not utopia by decree—just a species that stops tripping over its own cognitive furniture quite so often.
